title: Payment Processing Standard: Posting, Interest Accrual and Allocation
content:
This standard governs how payments post to Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts and how each payment is split between interest, fees and principal.

## 1. Where and when a payment posts

1.1 Payments post only to a contract whose status is active, as the contract record shows.

1.2 A payment made after the payment cutoff time, or on a weekend or US federal holiday, posts on the next business day.

1.3 Every posted payment sets the last payment date to its posting date.

## 2. Interest

2.1 Interest is daily simple interest: the principal balance times the APR in effect on the posting date, divided by the tier's day-count basis, times the days since the last payment, rounded to the cent.

2.2 The days since the last payment are the calendar days from the day after the last payment date through the posting date.

## 3. Allocation order

3.1 Each payment is applied in this order: accrued interest to the posting date, then outstanding fees oldest first, then principal. Interest takes no more than the payment; fees take no more than what remains of the payment after interest and no more than the fees due; principal takes the rest.

3.2 A principal-only payment, where the tier allows it, is accepted only when no installment is past due and goes entirely to principal.

3.3 A scheduled-installment payment advances the next due date by one month for each full monthly payment it contains, never beyond the maturity date — **this clause is no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for scheduled-installment payments and is not applied.

3.4 A partial payment is applied in the same order but never advances the next due date.

3.5 A payoff payment equal to the payoff amount brings principal, interest and fees to zero and closes the contract as paid off.

## 4. Channel fees and card limits

4.1 A one-time payment taken by a representative by phone bears the tier's agent-assisted payment fee, assessed with the payment and paid from it. Payments by autopay, online or mail bear no fee.

4.2 A single debit card payment may not exceed the tier's maximum debit card payment, and no more than the tier's maximum debit card payments may post in one calendar month, counting the contract's online and representative-assisted debit card payments posted in the calendar month of the posting date. The contract's payment history is the evidence.

## 5. Worked allocation (hypothetical figures)

Principal balance 12000.00, APR 9.09 percent, day-count basis 365 days, last payment date 30 days before the posting date, fees due 15.00, payment 400.00 made online:

| Step | Amount |
|---|---|
| Interest: 12000.00 times 9.09 percent, divided by 365, times 30 days, rounded | 89.65 |
| Fees: the lesser of 15.00 and what remains (310.35) | 15.00 |
| Principal: 400.00 less 89.65 less 15.00 | 295.35 |

The last payment date becomes the posting date. Had the same 400.00 been taken by a representative by phone, the agent-assisted payment fee would be assessed with the payment and paid from it.

superseded_clauses: A scheduled-installment payment advances the next due date by one month for each full monthly payment it contains, never beyond the maturity date;
